messages:
katie: quick heads-up — onboarding gemma-lite -> qwen-compat conversion, quantized int4, seeing large quality drop for >2k tokens. short answers OK, long-context summaries drift and hallucinate. suspect rotary index or token id aliasing. Anyone seen this pattern?

anil: which conversion script/version? and are you using our head-permute shim?

katie: using tools/convert_gemma_to_qwen.py v0.9 (internal). no head-permute shim. ran a diff of token ids for some sentinels and found odd mapping: 
```
# tokenizer mapping excerpt
orig_id: 50255 -> byte_seq: 0xE2 0x80 0x8B (ZWSP)
converted_id: 50255 -> byte_seq: 0xE2 0x80 0x8C (ZERO WIDTH NON-JOINER)
```
so same id but different bytes for a handful of high ids. also noticed rotor/rotary phase mismatch warnings in the loader: "rotary_dim != expected_head_dim" but it loads anyway.

maria: can you paste eval diffs? short metric + long-context metric?

katie: quick stats from ri-bench (same prompts pre/post):
```
- short (<=128): exact_match delta -0.7%
- mid (512): exact_match delta -3.4%
- long (2k+): exact_match delta -18.9%
- rouge-l long: -12.3 points
```
bench-bot: automated regression alert: suite=rotary-longctx, severity=high, trace_id=rb-44321

anil: that magnitude screams kv-cache misindexing or rotary head dim off-by-one per-head. If the tokenizer produced different byte mapping but same ids, downstream embedding lookup could be stale (embedding file indexed by byte sequence hash). Did the conversion regenerate embedding index or reuse original index?

katie: I reused the original embed.bin to save time. perhaps that was dumb. repro command I ran:
```
convert_gemma_to_qwen.py --model gemma-lite-3b --out qwen-compat --quant int4 --reuse-embeds yes
ri-eval run --suite rotary-longctx --model qwen-compat-int4
```

sam: fwiw saw a similar symptom when headwise-rotary ordering changed between exports. We added a tiny shim that reorders per-head rotary params at load-time:
```
# pseudo
if rotary_layout == 'old':
  rotary = rotary.reshape(n_heads, head_dim)
  rotary = rotary[:, ::-1]  # reverse per-head layout
```
that fixed our head-phase drift.

maria: also check vocab normalization (NFKC/NFKD) differences — some diacritics can fold differently and appear as different bytes even though tokenizer id collision hides it. That explains ZWSP vs ZWNJ swap.

katie: tried two quick experiments: 1) regenerated embeddings from converted vocab -> got ~6% lift on long-context; 2) applied per-head rotary reorder -> another ~4% lift. still ~8% gap vs baseline.

anil: makes sense. next steps: 1) full embed regen (no reuse) 2) add a short conversion unit test that compares byte-level token -> byte_seq map before accepting conversion 3) run a head-dim sanity check to assert rotary_dim % head_dim == 0 and warn if mismatched.

katie: I can run full embed regen but it'll take a couple hours on a node. scheduling now.

maria: can we also add a small prompt set that stresses rare unicode diacritics + long prefix caching? add to regression harness.

katie: adding to ri-eval: `rotary-longctx-unicode` with 120 prompts. will kick off after embed regen.

deploy-bot: conversion job completed: qwen-compat-int4 (run-id cv-77892) — artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-artifacts/cv-77892/

sam: ping me if you want me to run binary diff of rotary params vs original gemma dump. I have a small script that checks per-head sign/stride.

anil: also as a short-term mitigation we can enable fallback routing in the console: route long-context requests to dedicated gemma-hosted pool until conversion passes. avoids customer impact.

katie: thanks all. action items: (katie) regen embeddings + run `rotary-longctx-unicode` (in progress), (anil) add rotary/head-dim assertion to conversion script, (maria) add unicode stress suite to ri-eval, (sam) optional binary diff. I'll report back w/ numbers in this thread.

katie: quick interim note — after regen + shim reorder I'm down to 2.1% long-context delta, looks like the majority was embed/vocab mismatch. will follow up with full eval later tonight. :party_parrot:
